n: In the temple’s Court of the Women, Jesus watches wealthy people dropping their gifts into the offering chests.

f.g: Thirteen trumpet-shaped offering chests stood in the Court of the Women.

n: He also sees a poor widow put in two tiny copper coins — the smallest money there was.

f.g: Two lepta, the smallest coins in circulation — a tiny fraction of a day’s wage.

n: Jesus declares that she has given more than all the rich donors combined. God measures gifts not by amount but by sacrifice and heart.

f.w: hath cast in more than they all

n: They gave from their surplus; she gave from her poverty — everything she had to live on. Her gift came at real cost. Just before, Jesus condemned those who “devour widows’ houses.”

f.w: all the living that she had
f.g: All she had to live on.

n: Some admire the temple’s beauty — its fine stones and donated decorations. Herod’s temple was one of the wonders of the ancient world.

f.g: Beautiful stones; some of Herod’s temple blocks were enormous, gleaming white limestone.
Votive offerings — gifts dedicated to adorn the temple.

n: Jesus warns that the day is coming when not one stone will be left standing on another. The Romans destroyed the temple in AD 70.

f.w: there shall not be left one stone upon another

n: The disciples ask when this will happen and what sign will warn them. Jesus’ answer blends the coming fall of Jerusalem with the signs of His Second Coming.
First warning: don’t be deceived. Many will come claiming to be the Christ or saying the end is near. Don’t follow them.

f.w: many shall come in my name

n: Wars and uprisings will happen, but don’t panic. These must come first, but the end won’t come immediately.
Nations and kingdoms will fight one another.
There will be great earthquakes, famines, plagues, and terrifying signs in the heavens.
Before all this, disciples will be arrested and persecuted, handed over to synagogues and prisons, and put on trial before kings and governors. The book of Acts records many such trials.
These trials will become opportunities to bear witness of Christ.
So decide in advance not to worry about preparing a defense.

f.g: Rehearse or prepare a speech beforehand.

n: Jesus Himself will give them words and wisdom no opponent can refute or resist. Stephen experienced exactly this.

f.w: I will give you a mouth and wisdom

n: Betrayal will come even from parents, siblings, relatives, and friends. Some disciples will be killed.
They will be hated everywhere because they bear Christ’s name.
Yet not a hair of their heads will perish. Even if they are killed, nothing of eternal value will be lost.

f.w: not an hair of your head perish

n: By patient endurance they will gain — or keep — their souls. Steadfastness is the path to eternal life.

f.w: In your patience possess ye your souls
f.g: By enduring, you will gain your lives.

n: When armies surround Jerusalem, they will know its destruction is near. Roman legions besieged the city in AD 70.
That will be the signal to flee to the mountains and not to enter the city. Early Christian tradition says believers heeded this and escaped to Pella, east of the Jordan.
These are days of judgment, when everything the prophets warned about will be fulfilled.
It will be especially hard for pregnant women and nursing mothers, who cannot flee easily. Great suffering will fall on the land.

Many will die by the sword or be taken captive to other nations. Jerusalem will be dominated by Gentiles until the “times of the Gentiles” — the era when the gospel goes primarily to them — is complete.

f.w: the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled

n: Now Jesus looks further ahead: signs in the sun, moon, and stars, nations in anguish and confusion, and the roaring of the sea and waves.

f.w: signs in the sun, and in the moon

f.g: Bewilderment, not knowing which way to turn.

n: People will faint with terror at what is coming on the world, as the very powers of heaven are shaken.

f.w: Men's hearts failing them for fear

n: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory — Daniel’s vision fulfilled.

f.w: the Son of man coming in a cloud

n: For the faithful these signs are not cause for terror but for hope. Stand tall and look up — your deliverance is near!
Jesus gives a parable: look at the fig tree and all the trees.
When they sprout leaves, you know summer is near. You don’t need anyone to tell you.
Likewise, when you see these signs, you’ll know God’s kingdom is near. The righteous can read the signs of the times.

f.w: the kingdom of God is nigh at hand

n: “This generation” will see these things fulfilled. Interpreters understand this in various ways — the generation that saw Jerusalem fall, or the generation that sees the final signs begin.

f.w: This generation shall not pass away

n: Heaven and earth will pass away, but Christ’s words will never fail. His promises are more certain than the universe itself.

f.w: my words shall not pass away

n: Be careful that your hearts aren’t weighed down by overindulgence, drunkenness, and life’s worries, so that the day catches you off guard.

f.g: Overindulgence; the hangover that follows a binge.

n: That day will spring like a trap on everyone on earth who is unprepared.
So stay alert and pray constantly, that you may have strength to come through it all and stand confidently before the Son of Man.

f.w: Watch ye therefore, and pray always
to stand before the Son of man

n: During this final week, Jesus taught in the temple each day and spent His nights on the Mount of Olives.

f.g: Stayed — perhaps camping, or lodging at Bethany on the far slope.

n: People came early each morning to hear Him in the temple. His last days were spent teaching.

f.g: They rose at dawn to hear Him.
